correctness.rationale: For vertex sets of size at most four, a one-step hazard estimate yields a uniform power-law survival bound. For a fixed forbidden edge, exact algebra compares the real transition to the isolated-missing-edge reference. Triple and four-vertex survival bounds control each step perturbation by \(O(s/N^3)\); reference factors telescope to \(3/(N^2-1)\), and the accumulated error is \(O(\log N/N^3)\). Degree-two forbidden graphs guarantee that failure occurs exactly when the last pair is forbidden. The standalone exact-rational checker passed 28,833 assertions; those finite checks corroborate but do not establish the analytic uniform limit.

originality.rationale: The accessible full Arnosti paper provides randomized-algorithm comparisons on random bipartite graphs, not a shape-uniform fixed-complement rare-failure law. The Dyer-Frieze algorithm introduction is broader in domain but its accessible abstract describes worst-case guarantees and forests, not an equivalent estimate. A previous symmetric deleted-matching special case does not imply the present uniform theorem for deleted paths/cycles. Plausible historical coverage in inaccessible material remains a risk.

value.rationale: The theorem proves shape-universality for rare greedy-matching failure across arbitrary degree-two forbidden subgraphs: the leading failure probability depends only on the number of missing edges, is 3/2 times naive uniform-pair sampling, and the location of the failure becomes asymptotically uniform. This is a natural reliability statistic not supplied by approximate matching-size ratios; the moment method genuinely handles lack of symmetry and dependence across all path/cycle configurations.
